current.text: Phoenix sees Green as its starting point guard. He has played point guard in preseason and is asked to bring the ball up.
Experts doubt the point guard plan. They call it a strange choice for a player with little vision, and Josh thinks Booker will run the offense.
He is a projected starter next to Devin Booker, Dillon Brooks, Miles Bridges and Oso Ighodaro. Collin Gillespie comes off the bench.
Booker, Brooks and Bridges also need touches, so the Phoenix usage is crowded.

His low minutes last season came from minutes limits after his hamstring injuries, not from his role. Experts expect 30 to 33 minutes this season, with usage dropping a little from 32% to about 28 to 29%.
Experts project about 20 points and two or more threes a game, with about 4 rebounds and 4 assists.
His FT% (75%) and 3P% (31%) from last season should probably rise back toward his earlier 81% and 35%.
His steal rate last season came from an unusually high share of deflections turning into steals. Experts call it luck and do not expect it to hold.
In category leagues he fits around rank 100 to 110 if he reaches about 21 points and 4 assists.
In recent 12-team category mocks experts took him in round 9 for a scoring boost and in round 10 as a flyer.
Yahoo lists him as questionable for rest. Experts say last season's hamstring is not a concern.
Phoenix has the best fantasy schedule in the league: 4, 4 and 4 games in our playoff weeks and the fewest back-to-backs.

durable.text: He is a high-volume scorer who can score 20 or more points a game with over two threes. He took a huge number of shots at 32% usage when healthy last season.
His FG% is poor on high volume and hurts a team's FG% clearly. He plays downhill but is not efficient around the rim.
Outside scoring and threes his line is thin: few steals, few blocks and poor rebounding.
He is a weak passer with low basketball IQ who has never shown point guard skills.
His turnovers are high for his position.
9-cat formulas punish his poor efficiency, so he is worth more in points leagues than in category leagues.
He had never been hurt before 2025-26. That season he had three hamstring strains and played 32 games.

tags.name: injury prone
tags.detail: three hamstring strains in 2025-26; no injuries before that, and experts call the hamstring not a concern now

tags.name: injury last season
tags.detail: 32 games at 26 minutes after hamstring strains

tags.name: bounce-back
tags.detail: more minutes, FT% and 3P% expected to recover

tags.name: role up
tags.detail: 30 to 33 minutes expected after minutes limits last season

note: Green is a late scoring pick for us. Yahoo values him at 0 USD (average cost 1.6 USD) and ESPN at 2 USD (average cost 2.4 USD), and our league paid 9 USD last season, so pay no more than a few dollars near rank 100 to 120. He suits punt FG% and punt TO builds, where his points and threes (projected 20.7 PTS and 2.7 3PM) count fully, and the 4-4-4 Phoenix playoff schedule adds value. Early in the season, check whether he keeps the point guard role, plays 30+ minutes and gets close to 4 assists, and whether his FT% climbs back toward 80%.
